QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_4

question.text: Mr. Arjun Kapoor, manager of Himalaya Private Equity Fund (Cat II), wants to amend the PPM to increase the management fee from 2.0% to 2.25% post-commitment period. The AIF has NOT obtained the 75% consent threshold. What process does SEBI mandate?

answer.text: The Manager must provide dissenting unit holders with a mandatory exit option (not less than 1 month dissent window, buy-out at average of 2 independent valuations, completed within 3 months).
The Manager can unilaterally amend the PPM so long as it is disclosed in the next quarterly report.
The Manager must liquidate the fund immediately and return capital to all investors.
The Manager must refer the matter to the National Company Law Tribunal under IBC 2016.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI Circular CIR/IMD/DF/14/2014 (subsumed into the July 2023 Master Circular), material PPM changes or change of Sponsor/Manager/control in a close-ended AIF trigger a mandatory exit right to dissenting unit holders unless 75% of unit holders by value approve. The process: 1-month dissent window, valuation by 2 independent valuers, exit at not less than average of the two, completed within 3 months, expenses borne by Manager/Sponsor. The Trap: Option B ignores the material-change regime entirely. Liquidation is reserved for true winding-up. NCLT / IBC is for insolvency, not commercial PPM amendments. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A distributor exam asks the LP-side: what should the client do if a change is announced? XIX-C covers the Manager's duty across all cats. XIX-D drills the exact mechanics. Manager's Pro-Tip: When drafting a fee-hike amendment, run the 75%-by-value poll FIRST. If you clear 75%, the mandatory exit process does not trigger. If you miss it, you face valuer cost plus 3-month distraction — and it usually signals LP dissatisfaction that bleeds into Fund II.
